options.text: There are literally no servers involved
You don't provision or manage servers — the provider runs and scales them, billed by use
Your code runs on your own laptop

questions.explanation: Serverless means you don't provision, manage, or patch servers; AWS runs and scales them and bills you by use. Servers still exist — you just don't manage them.

questions.prompt: What is AWS Lambda's maximum execution time for a single invocation?
questions.explanation: A Lambda invocation can run at most 15 minutes. Longer or heavy sustained work belongs on containers/EC2 or must be split into steps.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Lambda are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is event-driven — invoked by triggers like S3 uploads or API Gateway requests
It is stateless, so state must live in external stores
You are billed by requests plus duration, and idle functions cost nothing
It keeps data in memory reliably between invocations

questions.explanation: Lambda is event-driven, stateless, and billed by requests + duration with nothing charged when idle. It does NOT reliably retain in-memory state between invocations.

questions.prompt: Which workload is a POOR fit for Lambda?

options.text: Generating a thumbnail when an image is uploaded
A 40-minute continuous batch job in a single invocation

questions.explanation: A 40-minute continuous job exceeds Lambda's 15-minute limit; it should run on containers/EC2 or be decomposed into steps. The others are short, event-driven tasks that fit Lambda.

questions.prompt: The startup latency when a new Lambda execution environment must initialize is called a ____ start.
questions.explanation: A cold start is the extra latency to initialize a fresh execution environment after idle or when scaling; provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm to avoid it.

questions.prompt: Match each service to its role in a serverless application.

pairs.right: Exposes an HTTP API that invokes the backend
Runs the application logic on demand

questions.explanation: API Gateway is the HTTP front door, Lambda holds the logic, DynamoDB stores data, and the execution role gives the function least-privilege permissions.
